claims.title: The Saqqaq settle Greenland
claims.summary: The Saqqaq, the earliest known people in Greenland, migrated from Arctic North America and spread along the coasts as caribou and seal hunters, beginning more than four millennia of continuous Arctic settlement.

sources.label: Aasivissuit–Nipisat. Inuit Hunting Ground between Ice and Sea

claims.title: The Dorset (Tuniit) culture
claims.summary: The Dorset Paleo-Inuit, expert sea-mammal hunters known for their carved art, followed the Saqqaq and occupied Greenland's coasts through the long pre-Thule centuries.

sources.label: Aasivissuit–Nipisat. Inuit Hunting Ground between Ice and Sea

claims.title: Arrival of the Thule
claims.summary: The Thule people migrated eastward from Alaska with dog sleds, kayaks and whale-hunting technology, settling Greenland's coasts and becoming the direct ancestors of the modern Kalaallit (Greenlandic Inuit).

sources.label: Aasivissuit–Nipisat. Inuit Hunting Ground between Ice and Sea

claims.title: Erik the Red founds the Norse colony
claims.summary: Erik the Red, exiled from Iceland, led settlers to south-west Greenland and established the Eastern and Western Settlements, the first European colony on the island.

sources.label: Kujataa Greenland: Norse and Inuit Farming at the Edge of the Ice Cap

claims.title: Leif Erikson sails to Vinland
claims.summary: Erik's son Leif Erikson voyaged west from Greenland to North America, reaching the land the sagas called Vinland and becoming the first European known to have set foot on the American continent.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Greenland: From the Paleo-Inuit hunters of the high Arctic, through Erik the Red's lost Norse colony and two centuries of Danish rule, to a self-governing Kalaallit nation with a recognised right to independence.", terralore.co/country/GRL/chronicle#ev-1000-leif-erikson-sails-to-vinland, claim TL:GRL:event:1000:leif-erikson-sails-to-vinland, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Submission to the Norwegian crown
claims.summary: The Greenlanders accepted the sovereignty of the king of Norway, tying the colony to the Scandinavian crowns and, through later unions, ultimately to Denmark.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Greenland: From the Paleo-Inuit hunters of the high Arctic, through Erik the Red's lost Norse colony and two centuries of Danish rule, to a self-governing Kalaallit nation with a recognised right to independence.", terralore.co/country/GRL/chronicle#ev-1261-submission-to-the-norwegian-crown, claim TL:GRL:event:1261:submission-to-the-norwegian-crown, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Norse settlements vanish
claims.summary: A wedding at Hvalsey Church in 1408 is the last dated record of Norse Greenland; the Eastern Settlement was abandoned within decades, the colony's disappearance still debated and linked to the Little Ice Age.

sources.label: Kujataa Greenland: Norse and Inuit Farming at the Edge of the Ice Cap

claims.title: Hans Egede reaches Greenland
claims.summary: The Dano-Norwegian missionary Hans Egede landed in Greenland seeking the lost Norse colonists, found only Inuit, and founded a mission and trading post at Godthåb (Nuuk), beginning the Danish recolonisation.

claims.title: The royal trade monopoly
claims.summary: Denmark established the Royal Greenland Trading Department, granting the crown a strict monopoly over all trade with Greenland and sealing the colony off from foreign contact for nearly two centuries.

claims.title: Danish sovereignty confirmed
claims.summary: The Permanent Court of International Justice ruled in the Eastern Greenland case that Denmark held sovereignty over the whole island, rejecting Norway's occupation of the eastern coast.

sources.label: Legal Status of Eastern Greenland (Denmark v. Norway), Judgment, 5 April 1933

claims.title: Greenland under U.S. protection
claims.summary: With Denmark occupied, the Danish minister Henrik Kauffmann signed the Agreement Relating to the Defense of Greenland with the United States, placing the island under American protection and opening it to U.S. bases.

sources.label: A Guide to the History of Recognition, Diplomatic, and Consular Relations: Denmark

claims.title: Thule Air Base built
claims.summary: Under a 1951 NATO-era defence agreement, the United States constructed Thule Air Base in north-west Greenland, a major Cold War installation for bombers and early-warning radar, now the Pituffik Space Base.

claims.title: From colony to Danish county
claims.summary: The revised Danish constitution abolished Greenland's colonial status and made it an integral county of the Kingdom of Denmark, a change the United Nations accepted as decolonisation.

claims.title: Home Rule established
claims.summary: After a January 1979 referendum, the Home Rule Act came into force, giving Greenland its own parliament and government with Jonathan Motzfeldt as first premier and responsibility for many domestic affairs.

claims.title: Greenland leaves the European Community
claims.summary: Following a 1982 referendum, Greenland withdrew from the European Community in 1985, mainly to control its fishing waters, becoming the only territory ever to leave the bloc.

claims.title: Self-Government referendum
claims.summary: In a referendum some 75 per cent of Greenlandic voters approved the Self-Government arrangement, paving the way for greater autonomy and recognition of the right to self-determination.

claims.title: Act on Greenland Self-Government in force
claims.summary: The Self-Government Act came into force on Greenland's National Day, recognising the people of Greenland as a people under international law with the right to self-determination and a legal path to independence.

claims.title: Múte B. Egede becomes premier
claims.summary: After elections in 2021, Múte Bourup Egede of Inuit Ataqatigiit became premier, the youngest in Greenland's history, advocating independence as a long-term aim grounded in economic self-reliance.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Greenland: From the Paleo-Inuit hunters of the high Arctic, through Erik the Red's lost Norse colony and two centuries of Danish rule, to a self-governing Kalaallit nation with a recognised right to independence.", terralore.co/country/GRL/chronicle#ev-2021-mute-b-egede-becomes-premier, claim TL:GRL:event:2021:mute-b-egede-becomes-premier, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The 2025 election under world attention
claims.summary: Amid intense U.S. interest in the island, Greenlanders voted on 11 March 2025; the centre-right, gradualist Demokraatit party won the largest share, and most Greenlanders rejected becoming part of the United States.

claims.title: Jens-Frederik Nielsen becomes premier
claims.summary: Jens-Frederik Nielsen of Demokraatit took office as premier on 7 April 2025, supporting independence pursued pragmatically and insisting Greenland's future is for Greenlanders to decide.
